Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

SPECIFICATION FOR 
GLASS HONEY JARS 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope— Specifies requirements for glass jars for honey, 

2. Terminology — For the purpose of this standard, the terms covered in IS : 6654-1982 'Glossary of 
terms relating to glass containers {first revision )' shall apply. 

3. Nominal Capacity — The glass honey jars shall be of 100, 200, 500 and 1 000 g nominal capacity. 

4. Dimensions — As given in Table 1. 



TABLE 1 DIMENSIONS FOR GLASS HONEY JARS

5. IVIaterial — Jars shall be made from white flint glass. 

6. Brimful Capacity and Mass — As given below:

IS : 11369 - 1985 

6.1 The brimful capacity shall be tested in accordance with IS : 10497-1983 'Method of test for the 
determination of brimful capacity of glass containers by gravimetric method'. 

7. Neck Finish —The jars shall have roll on threaded pilferproof neck finish (see IS : 7511 
( Part 4 )-1986 Dimensions for neck finishes ; Part 4 Roll on sealed threads pilferproof ( ROSPP ) 
( first Revision ). The neck size for 100 g and 200 g jars shall be 38 mm and for 500 g and 1 000 g 
shall be 53 mm. 

Note — The transfer ring shown in the figure in Table 1 of IS : 7511 ( Part 4)-1986 Is not applicable to honey 
jars. 

8. Test 

8.1 Thermal Shock Resistance Test —The jars when subjected to the thermal shock test as per Method 
A given in IS : 6506-1972 'Methods for thermal shock tests on glassware' shall not show any visible 
cracks or damage after the test. The temperature difference (fi— tt) for the thermal shock test 
shall be kept at 35°C, keeping the lower bath temperature (t^) at room temperature. 

9. Marking and Packing 

9.1 Marking — Each jar shall be marked permanently and iegibiy on its surface or the bottom with the 
manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

9.1,1 IS! Certification Marking— Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

9.2 Packing — The jars shall be packed in accordance with the guidelines given in 13:6945-1973 
'Code of practice for packaging glass and glassware'.
